page: OVHcloud a10-45 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance engineered for compute-heavy parallel workloads and machine learning pipelines. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server provides 30 dedicated physical cores and 30 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9554 processor running at 3.3 GHz without hyperthreading. It incorporates 42 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.4 GB per core, along with 400 GB of bundled local SSD storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single dedicated NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPU equipped with 24 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational capabilities across integer, vector, and cryptographic routines. The AMD EPYC host processor achieves top-quartile performance in stress-ng single-core (3,108.08) and multi-core (93,542.95) tests, alongside high marks in PassMark CPU tests (60,981.57) and Clang software compilation (43,343.0). The processor also supports AVX-512 extensions, including VNNI and BF16 instructions, augmenting CPU-side inference and data processing. Cached memory operations register high read bandwidth, though larger uncached memory transfers and Geekbench multi-core metrics sit within average industry percentiles.

The instance delivers dedicated compute density by assigning 30 non-hyperthreaded physical cores paired with an enterprise tensor-core GPU. The primary architectural tradeoff is the constrained memory footprint, as 42 GB of system RAM provides a modest memory-to-core ratio of 1.4 GB per core. While adequate for GPU preprocessing and model serving, it limits workloads requiring substantial in-memory data structures. Furthermore, the instance includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external networking configurations for ingress traffic.

OVHcloud a10-45 is suited for AI inference, graphics virtualization, video transcoding, CI/CD code compilation suites, and parallel numerical simulations where dedicated CPU execution and GPU acceleration are required in a single host.
